title: Drummers Hard Yard and Cliff Jones
summary: He recalls a cheap drummer who bought whiskey for the band and Cliff Jones, who came up with him, played with Freddie Keppard and could play with six sticks.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Huh? Do you remember Bobby? Oh sure. Used to call him Hard Yard. Yeah.

He was a good drummer. Yeah. He went out there to California too. You there yet? That's another, no, I heard from him. But what was he? He was a good drummer. Yeah. He went out there to California too. You there yet? He said, I don't know, I heard from him. He said, what did you see there? He said, he'd dress up feet all the time. Yeah. He was a good little drummer. He was a cheap. Every time they come on the job, he'd buy the band a pint of whiskey, a quart of whiskey. You know, whiskey was cheap then, you know. And he was telling me, he'd do that. He'd get close all the time. Yeah. Good little drummer. He had a, my phone was like a hog. Oh, yeah. Oh my God. Did you tell me you didn't know Cliff Jones? Cliff Jones? Snaggs. Snaggs. Huh? Snaggs, the drummer. Cliff? Yeah. Cool, me and Cliff had come up together. I thought I asked him about that one. He went to Chicago. That's right. Then he come back there with some kind of disease, all broke out of his face. That's right. He got where he was back and died up there. That's right. He got a brother named Ring and he got a brother named Joe. Joe. Joe Jones. Yeah Cliff Jones. We come up together. Did you play with him? He was playing with Celestine a little while but when he come back here he couldn't catch her on his side. He'd been away for so long. He played with King Oliver a long time up there. Yeah. Ask him if he played. He was a good drummer too. Did you ever play with him? Yeah Cliff, yeah. What band? What band? He played with us now and then I think when he was just was learning. But he was good then. Yeah. He must be younger now. Cliff was younger all my age. He could do more with six sticks than anybody else. Take six sticks and never lose no time.
Boy one on his arm, one on his arm, one on his mouth, and two on his back part.

Yeah. He was a kid in his pocket. And boy he played all of them sticks. Was he there before you went up and on? No. Me and him worked together up there with Freddie Kepard. Oh yeah. And he taken sick and dying. Oh yeah. But he had something breaking out on him. Yeah. He's the one I told you to come on the job and say he left something behind me and he can't remember what it is. Uh huh. And he kept on thinking so he said oh that's right it's my teeth. I ain't got my teeth. Uh huh. That's false teeth and he left them under the pillow at his house. Ask him if he worked with Ike Morgan before he went to Mexico or after. Yeah did you work with Ike Morgan before you went to Mexico or after. I think.
